_note: THE TWO CLASSES THIS GATE RECOGNISES, declared as data so the next reader can check every forgiveness instead of trusting the code. Read by tests/test_ontology.py; the skeleton a new factory copies is docs/ontology-exemptions.example.json. `dated_artifacts` names DIRECTORIES whose files are DATED RECORDS — a survey, a score, a review written at an instant and never rewritten. A vocabulary gate cannot judge those: the banned word inside one is the evidence that the drift happened. They are EXCLUDED from judgement and COUNTED in the gate's own output, so an exclusion is never silent; a root here must be an existing directory, because a class whose root is absent excludes nothing and must not pass quietly. `exemptions` names ONE line inside a document that is NOT a dated record, where the banned term is QUOTED rather than used. Every entry carries all four fields — path, substring, reason, proof — because a path and a substring without a reason and a proof is forgiveness, not a declaration; `proof` points at a file and the line or section a reader can OPEN to check the quote. An entry matching 0 hits is STALE and fails the gate: an exemption excuses nothing once the line it named is gone. Paths are exact and matched literally, with NO globs, deliberately — an exemption cannot widen into a class. The roots and entries below are THIS factory's records; the kit ships the example file instead, because a member has neither these dated directories nor this history.
